solution: [Textbook misprint: the keyed option is printed as "bis (ethylenediamine dithiocyanatoplatinum (IV) ion" — the closing parenthesis after "ethylenediamine" is missing, so as set the ligand name runs into the metal name. It is preserved exactly as printed. The chapter's own Table 9.3 gives the correct form, "Bis(ethylenediamine)dithiocyanatoplatinum(IV)". The three distractors carry misprints too, also preserved: "dithiocyantoplatinate" for dithiocyanatoplatinate, "dicyanatobis" for dithiocyanatobis, "ethylenediammine" for ethylenediamine and "dithiocynato" for dithiocyanato. None of them affects the reasoning, which turns on "platinum" versus "platinate".]

Which of the following complexes exist as cis and trans isomers ?

1. \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_2Cl_4]^{\ominus}}\)
2. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]^{2\oplus}}\)
3. \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2Br_2]^{2\ominus}}\) (square planar)
4. \(\mathrm{[FeCl_2(NCS)_2]^{2\ominus}}\) (tetrahedral)
solution: [Textbook misprint: options (a) and (c) are printed CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER IDENTICAL — both read "1 and 3" — verified on the source page at high magnification. Since "1 and 3" is the correct answer, this question as printed has TWO correct options and a student choosing (c) is right on the chemistry. The options are preserved exactly as printed and the key is recorded on the first of the two identical choices. Almost certainly one of the two was meant to read a different pair, but the book does not say which, so nothing has been invented in its place.]
